source_refs.note: Topic 2.6.1, printed pages 32-33: the s orbital (Figure 2.5b, boundary surfaces of 1s and 2s).

blocks.text: The shape of an s orbital is spherical. The electron density around the nucleus in an s orbital is uniformly distributed in all directions. As the principal quantum number increases, the size of the s orbital becomes larger: the 2s orbital is a larger sphere than the 1s.

blocks.alt: Two sets of x, y and z axes. (a) The 1s orbital (n = 1, l = 0, m = 0) is a sphere centred on the nucleus. (b) The 2s orbital (n = 2, l = 0, m = 0) is a larger sphere with a smaller sphere inside, separated by a spherical node.
blocks.caption: The boundary surfaces of (a) 1s and (b) 2s orbitals (original diagram after Figure 2.5b).
